definition: Emotional insight is a clearer understanding of one’s own emotions, including recognizing feelings and reflecting on emotional and behavioral patterns. In this context, it refers to greater awareness of what someone is feeling and how those feelings relate to their responses.

reasons: The packet does not explicitly define “emotional insight” as “a clearer understanding of one’s own emotions,” even though it reports qualitative findings of “increased emotional insight” and secondary outcomes such as “emotional awareness” and “self-reflection.”

The definition’s specific phrasing that emotional insight includes “recognizing feelings and reflecting on emotional and behavioral patterns” is only partially supported: the packet mentions “emotional recognition” and that CBT aims to help adolescents “recognize emotional and behavioral patterns and reflect on their thoughts and responses,” but it does not directly link this description to the term “emotional insight.”

The definition’s statement that it refers to “greater awareness of what someone is feeling and how those feelings relate to their responses” is not explicitly supported in the packet as a definition of emotional insight.
